match.stem: Which iron ore mining area is correctly paired with the State in which it lies?
match.explanation: Bailadila is an iron ore range in Dantewada district (NCERT spells it Dantewara) of southern Chhattisgarh. NCERT says the Jharkhand belt 'further extends to Durg, Dantewara and Bailadila'; all three are in Chhattisgarh, and NCERT names Dalli and Rajhara, in the Durg area, among India's important iron ore mines. Chhattisgarh was carved out of Madhya Pradesh in 2000, so Bailadila is now in Chhattisgarh, not Madhya Pradesh; it is not in Karnataka or Maharashtra either. The other pairs are wrong: Noamundi (with Gua) is in Pashchimi Singhbhum, Jharkhand; Kudremukh is in Chikkamagaluru district, Karnataka; Gurumahisani is in Mayurbhanj district, Odisha.

questions.stem: The present level of urbanisation in world falls under which of following categories?
questions.reason: published bank question (wave 6 batch 2, 23 Nov 2026) states what the paper question needs; rewritten after the first was held, accepted by an independent audit, five blind solvers and five judges

match.stem:
Consider the following statements about the level of urbanisation.
(A) It is measured as the percentage of urban population to total population.
(B) India's level of urbanisation in 2011 was a little over 31 per cent.
(C) More than half of the world's population now lives in urban areas.
(D) In 2011, India's level of urbanisation was higher than the world's.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
match.explanation: NCERT measures the level of urbanisation as the percentage of urban population to total population, and gives India's level in 2011 as 31.16 per cent, which it calls quite low in comparison to developed countries; so (A) and (B) are true. NCERT also states that at present 55 per cent of the world's population lives in cities, a share estimated to rise to 68 per cent by 2050; so (C) is true. On each country's own definition of urban, more than half of the world's people have lived in urban areas since about 2007, so in 2011 the world's level was already a little over 50 per cent, far above India's 31 per cent, and (D) is false. Hence (A), (B) and (C) are correct. The world's present level of urbanisation (55 per cent in NCERT, a little under 60 per cent in the early 2020s) therefore lies between 50 and 75 per cent: well above India's, but below highly urbanised regions such as Northern America (about 82 per cent).

match.stem:
Arrange the following oil refineries of India from east to west.
(A) Digboi
(B) Mathura
(C) Bathinda
(D) Panipat
match.explanation: Place each refinery by its State and rough longitude. Digboi is in Assam (about 95.6 degrees E), the easternmost; it is NCERT's example of a field-based refinery. Mathura is in western Uttar Pradesh (about 77.7 degrees E). Panipat is in Haryana, a little west of Mathura (about 77 degrees E). Bathinda is in Punjab (about 75 degrees E), the westernmost of the four. East to west: Digboi, Mathura, Panipat, Bathinda, that is (A), (B), (D), (C). Barauni in Bihar (about 86 degrees E), NCERT's example of a market-based refinery, lies between Digboi and Mathura; Asia's first cross-country pipeline ran to it from Naharkatiya in Assam. So from west to east the line runs Bathinda, Panipat, Mathura, Barauni, Digboi. The order (C), (D), (B), (A) is west to east, the reverse of what is asked.

questions.stem: Which type of workers make up a large share of the total workforce in the high technology industry?

passage.title: Concept of High Technology Industry
passage.text: Concept of High Technology Industry - High technology, or simply high-tech, is the latest generation of manufacturing activities. It is best understood as the application of intensive research and development (R and D) efforts leading to the manufacture of products of an advanced scientific and engineering character. Professional (white collar) workers make up a large share of the total workforce. These highly skilled specialists greatly outnumber the actual production (blue collar) workers. Robotics on the assembly line, computer-aided design (CAD) and manufacturing, electronic controls of smelting and refining processes, and the constant development of new chemical and pharmaceutical products are notable examples of a high-tech industry. Neatly spaced, low, modern, dispersed, office-plant-lab buildings rather than massive assembly structures, factories and storage areas mark the high-tech industrial landscape. Planned business parks for high-tech start-ups have become part of regional and local development schemes. High-tech industries which are regionally concentrated, self-sustained and highly specialized are called technopolies. The Silicon Valley near San Francisco and Silicon Forest near Seattle are examples of technopolies.

match.stem: Which one of the following statements about technopolies is correct?
options: Their landscape is marked by massive assembly structures and large storage areas.
Silicon Forest, near Seattle, is a technopolis in the United States of America.
Blue-collar production workers greatly outnumber the white-collar specialists in them.
Silicon Valley and Silicon Forest are both technopolies in Canada.
match.explanation: Technopolies are high-tech industries that are regionally concentrated, self-sustained and highly specialised. NCERT's two examples are Silicon Valley near San Francisco and Silicon Forest near Seattle, and both are in the United States of America: San Francisco is in California, and Seattle is in Washington State, in the Pacific Northwest close to the Canadian border. The nickname Silicon Forest is most often used for the high-tech cluster around Portland, Oregon, the State just south of Washington, and that is in the USA too. So Silicon Forest is a technopolis of the USA, not of Canada. The landscape claim is wrong: the high-tech landscape has neatly spaced, low, modern office-plant-lab buildings rather than massive assembly structures and storage areas. The workforce claim is reversed: highly skilled white-collar specialists greatly outnumber the blue-collar production workers.

questions.stem: The Indian Railway was introduced in 1853 between which two places?

passage.title: Rail Transport
passage.text: Rail Transport The Indian Railways network is one of the longest in the world. It facilitates the movement of both freight and passengers and contributes to the growth of the economy. Mahatma Gandhi said, the Indian railways "...brought people of diverse cultures together to contribute to India's freedom struggle". The Indian Railway was introduced in 1853, when a line was constructed from Bombay to Thane, covering a distance of 34 km. Indian Railways is the largest government undertaking in the country. The length of the Indian Railways network was 67,956 km (Railway yearbook 2019-20). Its very large size puts a lot of pressure on a centralised railway management system. Thus, in India, the railway system has been divided into 17 zones. Indian Railways has launched an extensive programme to convert the metre and narrow gauges to broad gauge. Moreover, steam engines have been replaced by diesel and electric engines. This step has increased the speed, as well as the haulage capacity. The replacement of steam engines run by coal has also improved the environment of the stations. Metro rail has revolutionlised the urban transport system in India. Replacement of diesel buses by CNG-run vehicles along with the introduction of the metro is a welcome step towards controlling the air pollution in urban centres. Areas around towns, raw material producing areas and plantations and other commercial crops, hill stations and cantonment towns were well-connected by railways from the British colonial era. These were mostly developed for the exploitation of resources. After the Independence of the country, railway routes have been extended to other areas too. The most significant development has been the development of the Konkan Railway along the western coast, providing a direct link between Mumbai and Mangaluru. The railway continues to remain the main means of transport for the masses. The railway network is relatively less dense in the hill states, north eastern states, central parts of India and Rajasthan.

match.stem: Which railway gauge accounts for the largest share of the route length of Indian Railways?
match.explanation: Broad gauge (1,676 mm) carries most of the Indian Railways route length. Metre and narrow gauge cover much smaller shares, and dual gauge describes a track laid with two gauges rather than a separate gauge.

match.stem:
Consider the following statements about the zones of Indian Railways.
(A) The network is divided into zones because a network this large is hard to manage centrally.
(B) The North Central zone has its headquarters at Gorakhpur.
(C) The East Central zone has its headquarters at Hajipur, in Bihar.
(D) Kolkata is the headquarters of more than one zone.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
match.explanation: NCERT explains that the very large size of Indian Railways puts a lot of pressure on a centralised management system, and so the network has been divided into zones; its Table 7.2 lists 17 zones with their headquarters. The North Central zone is headquartered at Prayagraj in Uttar Pradesh; Gorakhpur, also in Uttar Pradesh, is the headquarters of the North Eastern zone, so (B) is false. The table gives Hajipur for the East Central zone; Hajipur, in Vaishali district across the Ganga from Patna, is in Bihar, and no other zone has its headquarters in that State. Kolkata, in West Bengal, is the headquarters of the Eastern zone, the South Eastern zone and the Metro Railway, so (D) is true. Hence (A), (C) and (D) are correct.
